_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC.

milestones.title: Marathon
milestones.detail: A Persian expedition is defeated. The war continues, and Persia remains the great power of the region.

milestones.title: A conventional end in the west
milestones.detail: Romulus Augustulus is deposed. The date is the usual marker for the end of the western emperors. The eastern empire continues.

milestones.title: An imperial claim in the west
milestones.detail: Charlemagne is crowned in Rome on 25 December. The claim is new, and Constantinople does not accept it as the only Roman empire.

milestones.title: Constantinople falls
milestones.detail: On 29 May the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II takes the city. The eastern Roman state ends. The same summer, Castillon ends the conventional Hundred Years' War.

milestones.title: Theses
milestones.detail: The Ninety-five Theses are dated 31 October. The story of a church door is later and is not established.

milestones.title: Westphalia
milestones.detail: The peace of 24 October adjusts the religious settlement of the empire. A theory of modern sovereignty is a later reading of it.

milestones.title: A summer of acts
milestones.detail: From the opening of the Estates-General on 5 May to the Declaration of 26 August, the French Revolution is a sequence. The republic is not one of those summer acts.

milestones.title: A year of revolutions
milestones.detail: Revolutions break out in many cities. The Communist Manifesto is published in London in February. Some results last, and many regimes do not.

milestones.title: War is declared
milestones.detail: From the assassination on 28 June to the British declaration on 4 August, the July crisis is a chain of choices under a mobilisation timetable.

milestones.title: Surrender, with two dates
milestones.detail: Germany surrenders at Reims on 7 May and at Karlshorst on 8 May. The Soviet Union marked 9 May. The murder of the Jews is part of what the war contained.

milestones.title: The Treaties of Rome
milestones.detail: On 25 March six states establish the European Economic Community. Membership is not a definition of the continent.

milestones.title: The Wall is opened
milestones.detail: On 9 November the Berlin Wall is opened. It is one event in a year of exits from communist rule, not the end of European argument.
